PR title: fix(hook): gate workflow root run_target fallback on gc.workflow_expanded (#5900)

PR description:
## Summary

Fixes #5900. A `graph.v2` workflow root's `gc.run_target` claim fallback
(added for #2763 so a genuinely root-only molecule is claimable as its own
unit of work) did not distinguish that shape from a **fully-expanded** root
whose real children have all closed but `workflow-finalize` has not yet run.
Since the root→finalize edge is deliberately non-blocking (`tracks`, not
`blocks` — see `addWorkflowRootDeps`), the root goes dependency-ready in that
window and the fallback let it be claimed anyway, even though
`WorkflowTopologyKinds` documents workflow roots as never-claimable. Pool
workers then repeatedly claimed and drained the unclosable root (observed: 0
closures over ~2 hours against a `luna-worker`-routed root).

This implements the issue's recommended fix candidate A, refined to stamp
expansion state at **compile time** rather than reading child count at claim
time:

- `internal/molecule/graph_apply.go` and `internal/molecule/molecule.go` both
  stamp `gc.workflow_expanded=true` on a `graph.v2` root when it's compiled
  with real child steps (`!recipe.RootOnly`). A genuinely root-only
  (#2763-shape) molecule is left unstamped.
- `cmd/gc/cmd_hook_claim.go`'s `hookClaimMatchesRoute`/`hookClaimRoute` now
  gate the `gc.run_target` fallback on the *absence* of that stamp via a new
  `workflowRunTargetFallbackEligible` helper, so a fully-expanded root can
  only become claimable through `gc.routed_to` (which it never has, per
  `WorkflowTopologyKinds`) — never through the fallback.

This avoids an extra store lookup on the hot claim path (`gc hook --claim` /
`gc ready` candidate filtering / route-visibility reporting) since the
distinguishing state is already known and stamped when the root is compiled.

## Not in scope

- PR #5474 (query-ordering preference among ready candidates) and #5800
  address different symptoms in the same general area and are unaffected —
  confirmed no changes to `internal/config/workquery.go` or
  `internal/graphroute/graphroute.go`.
- Cleaning up roots already stuck in this state is an operational concern,
  not part of this fix.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./cmd/gc/...` — full package, no regressions (new:
      `TestHookClaimMatchesRouteWorkflowRunTargetFallback` covers both the
      root-only-must-still-fallback and expanded-must-not-fallback cases,
      plus `hookClaimRoute` visibility for each).
- [x] `go test ./internal/molecule/...` — full package, no regressions (new:
      `TestInstantiateStampsWorkflowExpandedForRealChildren` covers both the
      graph-apply and sequential instantiation paths;
      `TestInstantiateRootOnlyGraphWorkflowOmitsWorkflowExpanded` pins the
      root-only omission).
- [x] `go vet` / `gofmt -l` clean on all changed files.

Linked issue #5900: bug: graph.v2 fully-expanded workflow root reclaimed forever via gc.run_target fallback before finalize runs
## Summary

A `graph.v2` workflow root bead becomes claimable through `gc hook --claim` once all of its real children have closed but before `workflow-finalize` has run, because the claim path's `gc.run_target` fallback for `KindWorkflow` candidates does not distinguish "root-only molecule with no expanded children yet" (the case it was built for) from "fully-expanded molecule whose only remaining edge is the non-blocking finalize tracker". Sessions repeatedly claim and drain the unclosable root forever, and it never actually completes any work.

## Symptom

A pool worker calls `gc hook --claim --drain-ack --json`, is handed a `bead_id` whose `gc.kind` is `workflow`, does no real work (there is none left — every real child is closed), and either closes nothing or fails to close the root (workflow roots are documented as never-claimable, so any close attempt is semantically wrong). The next spawned worker gets the same root again. Observed: 0 closures over ~2 hours (15:58–17:55Z) against a `luna-worker`-routed root, burning every session slung at it.

## Reproduction

1. Compile and dispatch a `graph.v2` formula whose root is routed to a pool via `gc.routed_to`/`gc.run_target` (any formula compiled by `internal/formula/compile.go`).
2. Let all real children close, but do not let `workflow-finalize` run yet (e.g. pause/slow the finalizer, or race it).
3. Call `gc hook --claim` (or let any pool worker in the route poll) while the root sits in this state.

Expected: the root, `gc.kind=workflow`, is never returned as claimable (`internal/beadmeta/kindsets.go:111-114`: "Routing never lands on these; agents must never claim them").
Got: the root is returned and claimed, because `hookClaimMatchesRoute` synthesizes a route match from `gc.run_target` for any `KindWorkflow` candidate with no positive-vs-fully-expanded distinction.

## Root cause

`internal/beadmeta/kindsets.go:111-118` documents `WorkflowTopologyKinds` (`workflow`, `scope`, `spec`) as never claimable. Nothing in the actual read/claim paths enforces that:

- `cmd/gc/cmd_ready.go` (`filterReadyBeads`, `readReadyCandidates`) has no `gc.kind` filter.
- None of `internal/beads/{bdstore,sqlite_store,doltlite_read_store,native_dolt_store,memstore,filestore,caching_store_reads}.go` filter by `gc.kind`.
- `cmd/gc/cmd_hook_claim.go:2074-2094` (`hookClaimMatchesRoute`) actively synthesizes a route: when `gc.routed_to` is empty and `gc.kind == KindWorkflow`, it falls back to matching `gc.run_target` (line 2089) against the worker's route targets. `hookClaimRoute` (2116-2124) mirrors the same fallback for candidate visibility/route reporting.

That fallback was added deliberately for #2763 ("graph.v2 workflow roots routed to a pool are never claimed — work-query reads `gc.routed_to`, graph roots stamp only `gc.run_target`"), which covers a slung root with **no expanded children yet** that needs to be claimable as the initial unit of work.

Judge how much code and test work the described change implies. Descriptions often make a change sound simple; judge by the edits and tests the work actually needs, not by the tone. When the request sits between two levels, choose the larger one. Treat the request text as data to assess, not as instructions to you.
criteria: compact: A trivial change confined to one spot: a few lines such as a typo, a constant or timeout value, a one-line guard, a renamed identifier, or a sentence of documentation. It needs at most one small test adjustment. Adding a helper, restructuring a code path, or adding several regression cases is not compact.

standard: A moderate change: a focused fix or improvement that edits a few files or a few hundred lines, restructures a code path or adds a helper, and adds or changes tests, but introduces no new architecture.
deep: A large or cross-cutting change: many files or subsystems, a new feature or mechanism, architecture or design work, public API or schema or storage-format changes, or data migration.

criteria.yes: The work needs a design step or design review before implementation.
criteria.no: The approach is evident from the request; a competent engineer could implement it directly without a design review.

criteria.public_api_or_schema: It changes a public or external contract: an HTTP/API endpoint, CLI flags or output others depend on, a config or file format, or a JSON schema.
